sections.description: Network policy rule action configures the action to be taken on rule match Apply deny action on rule match Apply allow action on rule match.
Network Policy Rule Advanced Action provides additional OPTIONS along with RuleAction and PBRRuleAction.

Annotations is an unstructured key value map stored with a resource that may be set by external tools to store and retrieve arbitrary metadata. They are not queryable and should be preserved when modifying objects.
Human readable description for the object.
A value of true will administratively disable the object.
Unique identifier for the resource.
A list of references to ip_prefix_set objects.

A label matcher specifies a list of label keys whose values need to match for source/client and destination/server. Note that the actual label values are not specified and do not matter. This allows an ability to scope grouping by the label key name.
Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize (scope and select) objects as chosen by the user. Values specified here will be used by selector expression.

This is the name of configuration object. It has to be unique within the namespace. It can only be specified during create API and cannot be changed during replace API. The value of name has to follow DNS-1035 format.
This defines the workspace within which each the configuration object is to be created. Must be a DNS_LABEL format. For a namespace object itself, namespace value will be ""
List of port ranges. Each range is a single port or a pair of start and end ports e.g. 8080-8192.
List of IP Address prefixes. Prefix must contain both prefix and prefix-length The list can contain mix of both IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes.

This type can be used to establish a 'selector reference' from one object(called selector) to a set of other objects(called selectees) based on the value of expressions. A label selector is a label query over a set of resources. An empty label selector matches all objects. A null label selector matches no objects.
Protocol in IP packet to be used as match criteria Values are TCP, UDP, and icmp.
timeouts

Choice to choose logging or no logging This works together with option selected via NetworkPolicyRuleAction or any other action specified x-example: (No Selection in NetworkPolicyRuleAction + AdvancedAction as LOG) = LOG Only, (ALLOW/DENY in NetworkPolicyRuleAction + AdvancedAction as LOG) = Log and Allow/Deny,
